prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim. Injury: knee injury. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1362; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following report of a sideswipe collision during a lane change on a multi-lane roadway. Insured vehicle contacted the claimant's vehicle on the driver's side rear quarter panel. Both drivers reported at the scene. Liability questions to be reviewed once statements are collected.

Entry 2: Recorded statement taken from the insured driver. Insured states they signaled and checked mirrors but the other vehicle moved into the lane as they were completing the change. Insured reports no prior incidents on this policy. Photos of both vehicles requested and received.

Entry 3: Contacted the claimant by phone. Claimant is not represented by an attorney and confirmed they are handling the matter directly. Claimant describes a knee injury from striking the interior door panel during impact and has been seen by a medical provider. Requested medical records and a signed authorization for release of information. Explained the claims process and the claimant's right to obtain their own estimates for vehicle repair.

Entry 4: Reviewed the photos and the preliminary repair estimate. Damage is consistent with a sideswipe contact on the driver's side. Independent appraisal scheduled. Medical documentation not yet received; claimant advised that a follow-up call will be made once records arrive. Witness statement from a passenger in the insured vehicle obtained and logged.

Entry 5: Medical records received and reviewed. Documentation supports a diagnosis of a knee contusion with follow-up recommended. Claim file updated with injury details. Liability assessment in progress, pending review of the scene diagram and the insured's statement. Supervisor notified that the injury component requires further evaluation before any settlement discussion.
